beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new, it's the module title

beats.trigger: You cannot really share an agent.
beats.got: Sharing an agent isn't a thing, I have to pick what actually travels: context, skill, output or interface.

beats.trigger: Write two or three sentences on what was switched on and what never followed.
beats.got: I'm supposed to have brought a failed rollout example. Easy for me, we have an unused portal, but I'd have liked to know this before the day.

beats.trigger: **Draft** a technical plan and a people plan side by side
beats.got: A list of verbs. Nothing new, but the people plan beside the tech plan is the part I care about.

beats.trigger: Pick one teammate who could use what your agent produces.
beats.got: Four ways to share. My pricing brief sounds like push, but my real problem, everyone keeping their own copy of the context files, sounds like strategy 1.

beats.trigger: You are not going to ask *"what should I share with my teammate?"*
beats.got: Start from the teammate's job, not from what I have built. Fair, that's how I'd do it as a consultant anyway.

beats.trigger: The test is specificity: does it name one teammate, their current way of doing the job, and an outcome you could observe?
beats.got: The agent read my files and wrote a job statement for one teammate, and I could check it for specificity. If it's generic, I send it back.

beats.trigger: If the reason is merely *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: I choose a sharing shape because it moves the teammate's outcome, not because it's easy for us to build.

beats.trigger: You now have the teammate's job and a candidate selected against it.
beats.got: nothing new, a handoff to the next exercise

beats.trigger: Now find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can actually absorb it, then draft both halves of the plan.
beats.got: Next step is the obstacle, then two plans.

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: The first technical limit I see is usually not the real blocker. Look for the one that explains the others, probably the political or habit one in my case.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: The people plan shows the gaps: owner, governance and who judges the output are mostly UNASSIGNED on my team. That's the useful finding.

beats.trigger: [Test the sharing plan](test-the-sharing-plan.md) checks the assumptions underneath these plans
beats.got: nothing new, a handoff

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: The plans are guesses until tested.

beats.trigger: *what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?*
beats.got: The question reframes adoption as what would have to be true for them to switch. It gives me two or three concrete tests for this week.

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.
beats.got: A pre-mortem that ends in one named person, one question and one test written to monday.md. That is usable on Monday.

beats.trigger: A candidate picked because it fits the infrastructure is shopping.
beats.got: nothing new, it's a recap of what I just did

beats.trigger: One law decides whether a sharing plan works.
beats.got: A lecture is coming that names the law.

beats.trigger: The two get reported as one number and they are not one thing.
beats.got: Licences and logins get reported as adoption, and that is exactly the number our leadership reads.

beats.trigger: The proposal got neither a yes nor a no.
beats.got: A real story of a good analysis dying because the deciders were not in it. It is the risk on my pricing decision, so I'm uncomfortable.

beats.trigger: They had not spent any of their own weeks inside it.
beats.got: The people who did the work took it in; the ones who only received the result didn't. So my CFO needs to be inside the work, not just get the memo.

beats.trigger: Accountability is the part with a name on it, and a name does not travel inside a folder.
beats.got: Context, boundary and checks copy; accountability doesn't. A bit abstract and nicely phrased, but I'd have to think about it before using it.

beats.trigger: The right choice is the one that fits the week your teammate already has.
beats.got: nothing new, I already had the four strategies and the absorption point twice

beats.trigger: Your candidate is not competing with nothing. It is competing with that.
beats.got: Same switch question from the exercise, now with examples (lands where they look, right first time, trusted person used it first).

beats.trigger: Send them a message today and ask for twenty minutes of their week.
beats.got: The plan stays a guess until that one person answers. Send the message today.

beats.trigger: Run this in the same session.
beats.got: One more prompt to review what I built.

beats.trigger: Access is a switch someone flips. Absorption happens in other people's weeks, at their pace, for their reasons.
beats.got: nothing new, a summary of what I already read

beats.trigger: **Bring what your Monday contact said, in their own words.**
beats.got: Come back with the real answer from the person, not my plan.

beats.trigger: Module 8 puts the agent to work on the building.
beats.got: The next module has the agent build things.

take_homes: Start from the teammate's actual job and what they use today, and pick the sharing shape from that, not from what we can easily build.
Write the people plan next to the tech plan. Empty owner and governance slots are the finding, and I have plenty on my team.
Giving people access isn't adoption. The ones who decide need to spend time in the work, or my pricing proposal gets a non-decision.

monday.move: Message one person from the pricing working group and ask for twenty minutes. Ask how they build the pilot-cohort view today, then test one assumption from assumptions.md: whether they would use the brief if it lands in the place they already look.
monday.who: One named pricing working group member (the module's file leaves the name for me to fill in)
monday.when: Message today, conversation early next week
monday.stop_condition: They tell me their current way works well enough and nothing in the brief beats it. Then I drop that candidate and don't build more.
monday.blocker: We have no shared place for the context files, so everyone keeps their own copy. I may have to sort that out before anyone else can pick up the brief.

misconception.why: The module never talked about prompts. It showed that what decides the outcome is who is inside the work and who owns it, so better prompts alone won't get the team there. I'm not fully convinced prompts matter less for my own output quality.

one_line: Useful if you want to get a team to actually use what you built. The people plan and the Monday message are the good parts, and the lecture repeats itself a bit.
